points.description: Notes that more than one routing-table entry can match the same destination address (for example, a /8 and a /16 can both match an address in the /8).
States that the longest matching prefix is the most specific route and that the router therefore selects it.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says the router selects the longest matching prefix but does not identify it as the most specific route.

levels.says: Says the router selects the longest matching prefix but does not explain that this is the most specific route.

points.description: Explains that choosing the longest prefix allows routes to be aggregated or summarized while still allowing more specific exceptions.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer mentions only route aggregation/summarization or only more specific exceptions, not both.

levels.says: Mentions only route aggregation/summarization or only the ability to have more specific exceptions, not both.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three ideas: multiple matching entries, longest prefix as the most specific route selected by the router, and the aggregation-with-exceptions benefit. Half credit is available on P2 for naming longest-prefix selection without the specificity reason, and on P3 for giving only one of aggregation or exceptions. No marks for merely defining a prefix or saying routers use routing tables without linking this to longest-prefix matching.
